rules.when: The task depends on fresh news, current events, live public facts, or recent market and product changes.
rules.why: Grok is the preferred dispatch when current web-connected context is central to the work.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest fast tier. The task is narrow and low ambiguity, so a strong model buys nothing and costs several times as much per turn.

rules.when: The task is routine implementation: a well-understood change with clear acceptance criteria, no design ambiguity, and an existing test seam to extend.
rules.why: Mid tier. This is the cheapest profile that still drives a full validation pipeline end to end, and most ship tasks land here rather than in the strong tier.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Strong tier. Firstmate compares every candidate with current relevant quota before dispatch, so use a strong coding profile.
